description:
Kernel auto-selection v2 rollout plan is a cross-functional engineering + product initiative at Redwood Inference to safely deploy a new generation of attention-kernel selection logic across Redwood’s serving runtime.

Goals:
- Improve p50/p95 latency and throughput for top model families (e.g., Llama-derivatives, Mistral/Mixtral-like MoE, Qwen-like, and long-context variants) by selecting the best attention kernel per request based on (model, GPU SKU, sequence lengths, kv-cache state, quantization profile, and batching regime).
- Reduce performance regressions and correctness risks by introducing explicit guardrails: per-model allow/deny lists, automated fallbacks to “known-good” kernels, and rollout policies tied to error/quality/perf metrics.
- Standardize the runtime’s kernel capability model and telemetry so SRE and Product Rollouts can run staged rollouts (shadow → canary → cohort expansion → default) in hosted, Dedicated, and (where possible) Private deployments.

Scope:
- Runtime changes: implement selection rules v2, kernel capability registry, and fallback behavior; add deep observability (kernel choice tags, perf counters, error signatures).
- Validation: benchmarking suite updates, perf canary coverage, and applied-ML regression checks (quality deltas due to numerical changes) for representative prompt sets.
- Rollout mechanics: feature flagging, cohort targeting by GPU+model, automatic rollback criteria, and documentation/runbooks.

Non-goals:
- Writing brand-new attention kernels from scratch for every architecture (v2 focuses on selection + guardrails; kernel R&D continues independently).
- Customer-facing API changes (selection is internal; only optional advanced knobs may be exposed later).

Key stakeholders:
- Runtime Kernels: Hiro Tanaka (EM), Grace Kim, Yuki Sato, Isabella Rossi
- Runtime Execution/Scheduling: Mateo Alvarez (VP), Sofia Ivanova (EM), Noah Patel, Omar El‑Sayed, Lena Fischer
- Release Engineering: Connor O’Brien, Sahana Iyer
- SRE/Observability: Neha Kapoor, Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Allison Grant
- Product (Console & Rollouts): Marissa Cole, Paula Mendes
- Customer Success (comms/escalations): Miguel Santos, Aparna Reddy
- Security/Compliance (mainly for Private rollout notes/auditability): Marcus Lin, Olga Petrov (consulted)

Timeline (representative):
- Phase 0 (1–2 weeks): requirements, metrics definition, and capability registry design.
- Phase 1 (2–4 weeks): implement selection v2 + telemetry; expand benchmark & perf-canary coverage.
- Phase 2 (2–3 weeks): shadow and canary in hosted; cohort expansion by model family + GPU.
- Phase 3 (2–4 weeks): enable for Dedicated customers (opt-in → default), publish runbooks, and prepare Private guidance/upgrade notes.

Deliverables:
- Design/ADR for selection rules v2 and guardrails.
- Benchmark + perf-canary reports proving wins and identifying risk areas.
- Rollout plan with explicit gates and automated rollback.
- Incident/oncall runbooks and a known-issues page for kernel selection.
- Implementation PRs across runtime, perf tooling, observability pack, and docs.

Constraints & risk management:
- Numerical differences across kernels can cause subtle output drift; applied-ML quality checks must gate rollout.
- Some GPU SKUs/driver versions may have kernel-specific failures; selection must include hardware-aware deny rules.
- Must maintain strong fallback guarantees to preserve platform reliability and customer SLAs during rollout.

files.description: Primary design doc: selection v2 algorithm, inputs/signals, capability registry format, rule evaluation order, fallbacks, and compatibility matrix by model family and GPU SKU. Includes open questions and phased rollout plan.

ADR capturing the decision to move from static per-model defaults to rule-based selection with guardrails; alternatives considered (manual pinning, per-release hardcoding), and rationale for safety mechanisms.
Benchmark methodology: workloads (short/long, prefill-heavy vs decode-heavy), metrics, test matrix (models x seq-lens x batch regimes x GPUs), and pass/fail gates for rollout.
Telemetry and dashboard spec: kernel-choice tags, per-kernel latency histograms, error signatures, fallback rate, GPU utilization, and SLO-aligned alerts/rollup views for canary analysis.

Operational rollout gates: shadow vs canary criteria, automated rollback thresholds (5xx, CUDA errors, p95 regression), and procedures for reducing blast radius (cohort targeting by model/GPU/region).
Living document listing known kernel-specific failures, GPU-driver quirks, model-family edge cases, and temporary deny-list rules; links to tickets/PRs and mitigation guidance.
Runtime release note draft: what changed, default behavior, how to override/pin kernels (internal), rollout status, and guidance for support/SRE during initial enablement.
PRD from Console & Rollouts: success metrics, customer impact framing (latency/cost), rollout controls needed in console/ops tooling, and communication expectations for Dedicated/Private.

Epic/parent issue: “Kernel auto-selection v2 rollout”. Breaks down into sub-issues for capability registry, rule engine, telemetry, perf-canary expansion, and rollout tooling. Includes definition of done and risk log.
Implement capability registry in runtime: schema, loading, versioning, and how kernels declare supported shapes/constraints; includes unit tests and integration test plan.
Selection rule engine v2: rule evaluation, scoring, tie-breakers, deny/allow lists, and safe fallback logic; includes acceptance criteria for correctness and determinism.
Runtime telemetry: add kernel_choice tag and fallback_reason; ensure metrics cardinality is bounded; add tracing spans for selection decision and kernel execution.
Perf-canary coverage: add new scenarios for long-context and MoE; ensure nightly runs across A100/H100/L4 (as available) and publish regression diffs.
Rollout policy requirements: cohort targeting fields (model family, quant profile, GPU, region), gating metrics, and rollback automation expectations; links to Confluence PRD and SRE gate doc.
PR: Add kernel capability registry and versioned manifests to runtime; includes schema, loader, and initial manifests for top model families; reviewers from runtime kernels + scheduling.
PR: Implement selection rules v2 (scoring + guardrails) behind feature flag; adds fallback paths, deny-list hooks, and logging; includes benchmarks summary in PR description.
PR: Add kernel-choice metrics/tracing and wire into observability pipeline; includes example dashboard screenshots/stubs and CI performance test results.
PR: Expand perf-canary suites for kernel selection v2; adds long-context and decode-heavy workloads, plus automated comparison reports for canary gating.
PR: Add dashboards/alerts for kernel selection v2 (fallback rate, per-kernel p95, CUDA error spikes) with recommended thresholds for canary rollouts.
Thread coordinating final selection heuristics for Llama-family and long-context: debate about tie-breakers, deny-list defaults, and what telemetry is required before canary.
Thread defining rollout gates and alerting: which metrics trigger rollback, how to segment by GPU/region, and who is on point during the first 24h of canary.
Thread between Product Rollouts and Runtime: aligning on console exposure (internal-only flags vs customer-visible), comms for Dedicated customers, and release timing.
Thread for a canary incident (e.g., increased CUDA illegal memory access on one GPU/driver combo): triage notes, mitigation via deny-list, and links to hotfix PR + dashboards.

Support ticket from a Dedicated customer reporting a latency regression after enabling a new runtime build; includes environment details, affected model, and coordination with SRE/runtime to confirm kernel selection behavior.
Email thread drafting customer communication for Dedicated enablement: what’s changing, expected benefits, opt-out/pinning guidance, monitoring period, and escalation path.
Kickoff notes doc: attendees, goals, initial risks, ownership, and milestone dates; links out to Linear epic and Confluence design/ADR.
Spreadsheet of week-1 canary results: p50/p95 deltas by model/GPU/region, fallback rates, error counts, and notes on anomalies; used to decide cohort expansion.
Transcribed design review meeting: runtime kernels + scheduling + SRE; decisions on guardrails, rollout stages, and test plan; action items and owners.
